1.0 Purpose
This Method Statement defines the safe and controlled procedure for pulling, positioning, and installing firefighting
pipes onto the main pipe rack and its branches for the Project. It is issued to the Consultant / Owner's representative
for review and approval prior to commencement of the activity and shall be read in conjunction with the applicable
project specifications, approved drawings, material submittals, the project HSE Plan and the site-specific Risk
Assessment.
2.0 Scope of Work
SIAC will take delivery of pipe materials from the approved supplier, store them in accordance with the
manufacturers' and suppliers' recommendations, and install them on the main pipe rack in accordance with the
approved schedule of installation methods. The installation shall be inspected for compliance with the relevant
project requirements and applicable international standards.
All manpower and materials employed in the installation shall be of the required skill and quality and shall conform
to the reference standards; where an item is not fully covered by the contract specifications, the best modern industry
practice, as determined and approved by the Engineer, shall apply.
3.0 References / Codes & Standards
The work shall be executed in accordance with, but not limited to, the following references:
• Approved project drawings, piping isometrics and material submittals.
• Project Contract Specifications and Owner's technical requirements.
• Project Health, Safety & Environment (HSE) Plan.
• Manufacturer's / supplier's storage, handling, and installation recommendations.
• Applicable local and international lifting/rigging safety regulations.
• Approved Rigging & Lifting Plan and supporting lift calculations for this activity.

7.0 Methodology / Sequence of Work
7.1 Pre-Work Preparations
1. Obtain approved Permit to Work / Lifting Permit and confirm this MOS, JSA and Lifting Plan have been
approved.
2. Conduct toolbox talk with all involved personnel, covering the task sequence, hazards, and controls.
3. Inspect and barricade the work area beneath the pipe rack to establish an exclusion zone, post warning
signage.
4. Inspect all rigging equipment (chain blocks, Rachit, slings, shackles) and confirm certification / SWL tags are
valid.
5. Install and secure rollers on the pipe rack branch prior to lifting the pipes (4 no. rollers per 12 m span, at the
designated fixing points).
This branch has two levels; the largest diameter pipe is 200 mm C.S. Sch. 40 (approx. 280 kg for a 6 m length). Lifting
in this direction is performed using two chain blocks of 3-ton capacity together with a 3-ton capacity Rachit.
1. Secure the pipe by hanging it from the 1st (fixed) suspension point on the branch using a chain block.
2. Wrap the pipe from the inside using the wire rope connected to the Rachit (3-ton capacity).
3. Unhook the pipe from the 2nd (external) suspension point near the branch, while keeping the 1st point
secured.
4. Begin pulling the pipe from inside the pipe rack in a slow, controlled manner using the Rachit.
5. Once approximately two-thirds (2/3) of the pipe length are inside the pipe rack, release the 2nd external
hanging point.
6. Continue rolling the pipe on the installed roller supports up to its final position on the pipe rack.
7. Once in final position, secure the pipe on its permanent supports as per the approved drawings before
releasing all rigging.
Notes – Roller System
• Rollers are mounted on the pipe rack branch before the pipes are lifted.
• 4 no. rollers are installed along each 12 m span, at defined fixing points.
• Each roller is designed for a working load of 580 kg (see attached design calculation).
• Stress analysis of the roller mechanism confirms a failure load of 1,070 Ton per roller, providing a substantial
safety margin over the working load.

8.0 Lifting & Rigging Requirements
• All lifting operations shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the approved project Lifting Plan and
calculations.
• All lifting gear (chain blocks, Rachit, slings, shackles) shall be third-party certified, color-coded and within the
current inspection validity, with SWL clearly tagged.
• No load shall exceed the rated SWL of the chain blocks (3 Ton), Rachit (3 Ton), or rollers (580 kg each) at any
point in the operation.
• A banksman/signalman shall direct all crane movements; only trained and authorized personnel shall operate
lifting equipment.
• The exclusion zone beneath the suspended/rolling load shall be always maintained and monitored by the
Safety Officer.
9.0 Quality Control & Inspection
• Verify pipe material, size, and schedule against the approved material submittal prior to installation.
• Inspect rollers and supports for correct installation and secure fixing before pulling commences.
• Visually inspect pipe surface/coating after pulling for any damage caused during the operation.
• Confirm final pipe position, alignment and support fixing against the approved drawings; record on the
applicable inspection/ITP checklist.
• Any non-conformance shall be recorded and closed out prior to proceeding to the next branch/section.

Actions to be taken in case of emergency.

• All the site workers must be trained on the site ERP. • The emergency phone numbers must be well known by all the site workers and posted at different locations on site. • The rescue team must be always ready on call, with the rescue equipment. • All the rescue tools (fire extinguishers, eye wash, stretcher, first aid kit...etc), must be inspected in a daily basis and ready to be used. • All the workers must be reminded about the nearest assembly points and the escape routes, prior to the start of the activity. In case of fire: • Eyewitness tends to extinguish the fire by himself (if he trained for) and informs his direct supervisor about that fact. • The direct supervisor must proceed to the area of fire, assess the situation, and inform the Project & HSE Managers about the fire. • The ERT (Emergency Response Team) shall arrive and apply the ERP rules. In case of medical emergency: • The first person to witness shall warn his supervisor and ask for assistance. • In case the Medical Emergency is due to an accident, check your own safety before approaching the scene of the accident. • Remove the victim to a safer place ONLY in case there is a chance of further injury; else do not touch the victim unless trained to do so. • If you are an approved First Aider, provide first aid, else wait till a Fist Aider or the site nurse arrives and provides first aid as appropriate. • Continue First Aid treatment till the Male Nurse / Medical Team arrives and takes care
